final.memo:
Our thesis for CoStar Group rests on the transition from an aggressive, acquisition-heavy growth model to one defined by spending accountability and the disciplined allocation of commercial cash flows [D01]. The April governance settlement provided the essential catalyst to oversee this shift, particularly regarding the residential investment segment [D01, D07]. As of year-end 2025, the framework is active, and management continues to report strong booking numbers, such as the $84 million in net new bookings reported for Q3 2025 [D03].

However, we remain in a period of patient observation. While revenue growth is evident, headline figures are insufficient to determine whether the residential business is becoming a profitable franchise or merely a permanent subsidy funded by the commercial segment [D02, D06]. We require a clearer bridge between bookings and segment cash earnings to validate the original thesis [D02, D03]. The skepticism remains that management may attempt to obscure segment-level returns to continue its current trajectory [D05, D06].

We maintain our position (HOLD) to see how the refreshed board and its capital-allocation committee execute the next phase of the plan [D01, D07]. We have not yet reached the point where the catalyst is spent, nor has the thesis been broken by a definitive refusal to act [D03, D05]. We will continue to monitor net new bookings and evidence of improved spending accountability as the primary gauges for whether the governance intervention is effectively constraining capital intensity [D02, D03].
